load_bearing_sub_hypothesis: H-c (whipsaw) primary; H-b (anti-selection on Sharpe dimension) secondary
operator_actionable_implications: Inverting the gating LOGIC alone would NOT recover positive edge — the cost-drag mechanism dominates the per-bar mean asymmetry. An invert-gate variant would still pay similar position-flip costs at every state transition (~30% of bars for ES).

A 'state-stability-confirmation' modification (gate fires only after N consecutive bars in state 1) would address H-c by reducing transition rate. Recommended exploratory variant: H050.stable-state with N in {5, 10, 20} bars of confirmation.

The 1-min cadence is structurally hostile to HMM gating because (a) costs are amortized over very small per-bar P/L and (b) HMM state transitions occur at the 1-min noise scale. Recommend exploring HMM gating at 5-min or 15-min cadence.
Multi-state HMM (n_states >= 3) might separate the within-vol-regime directional signal more cleanly than the current 2-state vol gate.

verdict.H-a_random_gating: REFUTED — per-state vol asymmetry empirically real (state 0 sigma 2.727e-04 vs state 1 1.664e-04 for ES; NQ ratio = 3.08x). HMM is detecting a VOL regime, not random. Random-gating null incompatible with the systematic 1.5x-3x vol ratio.
verdict.H-b_anti_selection: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED — ES Delta_mu(state1 - full)=-7.412e-07 < 0 (anti-selective on the mean dimension); NQ Delta_mu=1.049e-07 > 0 (anti-selective is NOT supported on the mean dimension). HOWEVER, on the per-bar Sharpe dimension: ES SR_state1_uncond=-0.0147 vs SR_state0_uncond=0.0006; NQ SR_state1_uncond=-0.0017 vs SR_state0_uncond=-0.0013. The HMM gate keeps the state with WORSE Sharpe in both symbols → anti-selection on the Sharpe dimension is empirically supported on BOTH symbols.
verdict.H-c_whipsaw: STRONGLY SUPPORTED — ES has 102472 forced position transitions on 337837 OOS bars (30.33% transition rate). Mean state-1 (active) run length = 4.7 bars (median 3); NQ 79237 transitions on 673274 bars (11.77%). Mean cost-drag per bar: ES -3.171e-06, NQ -2.485e-06. ES cost-drag absolute magnitude (3.171e-06) exceeds full-path uncond mean magnitude (1.700e-06) — whipsaw alone fully explains the gated-arm catastrophe.
verdict.H-d_distribution_shift: WEAK — ES OOS P(state=1)=0.7159 vs train-implied stationary 0.7486 (shift -0.0327, relative -4.36%); NQ OOS P(state=1)=0.7618 vs stationary 0.7016 (shift +0.0602, relative +8.58%). Distribution shift is materially smaller than the whipsaw mechanism — H-d contributes marginally, NOT load-bearingly.
